title: By Faith We Find the Place Above
description: By Faith We Find the Place Above in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 64.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: By faith we find the place a-bove, The Rock that rent in twain; Be-neath the shade of di-vine love, And in the clefts re-main.

lines: By faith we find the place above,
The Rock that rent in twain;
Beneath the shade of divine love,
Jesus, to thy dear wounds we flee,
Assured that all who trust in thee
Then let the thundering trumpet sound,
The mountains melt, the solid ground
Yet still the Lord, the Saviour reigns,
So be it! let this system end,
And when thou dost in glory come,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
